scope: Current-canonical admission of candidate-bound bottom sensible-energy publication, transactional thermal provenance and external donor binding

invariants.evidence: Single SWAP kernel remains authoritative; bottom-energy accounting is an opt-in runtime/process capability, not a separate kernel version.
No file, format, path, parsing or file-unit dependency is introduced into kernel or EB source.
Energy parameters, transient thermal carrier data and publication results remain typed and separate from committed hydrologic state and forcing.
No bottom-energy data is added to compact persistent column state; publication is accepted-only runtime output.
Thermal carrier and attempt provenance are worker/transaction scratch through transaction_attempt_context_t and are cleared after trial handling.
No per-column storage-layout restriction is introduced; the opt-in seam is compatible with batched/logical-column runtime organization.
Thermal scratch participates in capture/restore; publication occurs only after accepted receipt provenance matches the prepared candidate; rejected trials publish nothing.
Warm-start and recomputation semantics are unchanged; thermal publication is derived from the exact trial candidate and does not become physical restart state.
Carrier samples and publication use generic t0/t1 intervals; no day, month, year or midnight boundary is introduced.
No fixed coupling-window duration is introduced; external donor requests carry the candidate/substep interval explicitly.
The explicit external thermal provider is coupling-compatible while transaction ownership and hydrologic acceptance remain in the existing runtime.
Groundwater head/flux interface semantics and q sign convention are unchanged; energy is bound to the already-accounted exact bottom water transfer.
No second water ledger or water transfer is created; F-VQ79 preserves hard mass closure with maximum observed absolute residual about 2.22e-16 cm.
No interface-sensitivity result or derivative semantics are altered.
Energy evaluation reuses the accepted hydraulic trajectory and thermal carrier; it does not require structural extra full SWAP runs.
MultiSWAP runtime is the publication owner; no heavy solver instance is added per logical column.
No MODFLOW cell/tile area-fraction knowledge is introduced into SWAP or EB source.
No deep-vadose transfer-zone ownership or state is introduced.
No deep-vadose/direct-coupling transition storage semantics are changed.
Common soil-water solver contracts remain unchanged; this admission does not make alternative soil-water solvers architecturally impossible.
Existing soil-temperature access and hydrologic transfer information are reused rather than duplicating soil/crop/ET/drainage physics.
EB modules consume typed runtime/process information and do not depend on HeadCalc internal arrays or numerical implementation details.
Bottom-energy capability activation and physical donor semantics remain separate from numerical solver/temporal policy; warning remediation introduced no policy change.
Qualified publication route preserves the bounded one-trajectory HeadCalc case; energy postprocessing adds no unbounded retry loop.
Full reference mode remains available and supplies the qualified production route used by the evidence.
Publication exposes energy status and provider complete/unavailable/stale/invalid counts while existing solver, retry and water-balance diagnostics remain intact.
Thermal carrier allocation is opt-in and additionally requires active soil temperature; unused columns do not acquire persistent EB state.
External donor temperature is supplied through runtime/provider composition; SWAP does not learn MODFLOW/tile/deep-vadose system topology.
No midnight, one-day, legacy-file or direct-MODFLOW assumption is introduced; interval identity and provider provenance are explicit.
F-CI63 audits all 30 invariants, locks exact production blobs and replays independent qualification before any promotion.
